name: Dating
description: You are the developer of a dating app which ignores gender completely. The app has $$$n$$$ users, indexed from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. Each user's profile features a list of the activities they enjoy doing. There are $$$m$$$ possible activities, indexed from $$$1$$$ to $$$m$$$. A match between two users is good if they share at least one activity and, at the same time, both of them like at least one activity that the other user does not like. Find a good match if it exists.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$2 \leq n \leq 200\,000$$$, $$$1 \leq m \leq 10^6$$$) — the number of users and the number of activities. Each of the following $$$n$$$ lines contains a number $$$k_i$$$ ($$$0 \leq k_i \leq m$$$) — the number of activities that user $$$i$$$ likes — followed by $$$k_i$$$ distinct integers from $$$1$$$ to $$$m$$$ — the activities user $$$i$$$ likes. It is guaranteed that $$$k_1+k_2+\cdots+k_n$$$ does not exceed $$$10^6$$$.
output_specification: Print $$$\texttt{YES}$$$ if a good match exists. Otherwise, print $$$\texttt{NO}$$$. If a good match exists, on the next line print two integers — the indexes of two users that make a match.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1949F — Dating [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
